title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay in expectations; value is what the asset base actually earns once the construction dust settles.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.html: At the TradingView close of ₹1,845.70 (session close ₹1,823.20 on 2026-11-13), Aurobindo holds a ₹1,06,212 crore market cap [1][23]. It trades at 26.1x TTM P/E, 2.69x book value (₹685), and a 0.38% dividend yield [1]. After rallying +52.51% from a ₹1,106.00 low to near its ₹1,859.90 high, the stock is no longer priced as a distressed generic [23]. Even so, it trades at a 29%–42% discount to large-cap peers at 36.5x–44.7x P/E [1]. That gap reflects its 12.9% ROCE (10.1% ROE) and active USFDA Warning Letters at Eugia Unit III and Unit I [1][8][9].

web_blocks.takeaway: Note on Source Reconciliation: The peer table above displays TradingView TTM P/E and ROE figures (26.8x, 41.4x, 39.1x, 41.5x, 17.7x, 45.2x), whereas Screener.in consolidated ratios report 26.1x, 36.9x, 36.5x, 41.6x, 16.3x, and 44.7x due to TTM vs. latest-FY / standalone-adjusted denominators [1][23][24][25][26][27][28]. Across both sources, Aurobindo trades at a sharp discount to Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's, and Gland Pharma because its 12.9% ROCE lags peers while Eugia carries USFDA Warning Letters [1][8][9].

web_blocks.html: A ten-year multiple check shows why 26.1x P/E sits in the upper half of Aurobindo's historical range [1]. During its FY15–FY18 peak-ROCE era (23%–27% ROCE), the stock traded at 18x–24x forward earnings [1]. In the FY22–FY23 trough (9%–10% ROCE), multiples fell to 11x–15x [1]. Today's 26.1x TTM P/E equals roughly 15.0x EV/EBITDA on a ₹1,03,210 crore enterprise value against ₹6,870 crore FY26 EBITDA [1][2]. That shows the market already credits Q2 FY27's record ₹10,263 crore sales run-rate [3].

web_blocks.takeaway: A Reverse DCF at ₹1,845.70 shows the market is pricing in ~11% 10-year revenue growth, 21% EBITDA margins, and a 400–500 bps ROCE recovery—fair for a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL asset, leaving thin margin of safety at CMP [1][23].

web_blocks.title: Why Peer Discounts Exist—And Why Lupin's 16.3x P/E Complicates Relative Value
paragraphs: On headline P/E alone, Aurobindo (26.1x) looks cheaper than Sun Pharma (36.9x), Cipla (36.5x), Dr. Reddy's (41.6x), and Gland Pharma (44.7x) [1][24][25][26][28]. However, Sun Pharma earns 20.5% ROCE with a strong US specialty book [24]. Aurobindo's 12.9% ROCE and 10.1% ROE still carry the weight of ₹24,902 Cr in fixed assets and 326-day inventory [1].

Meanwhile, Lupin trades at just 16.3x P/E with 29.9% ROCE and 28.7% ROE, though it sits in Stage 1 consolidation below its 200D SMA (₹2,233.94) [27]. Aurobindo will only re-rate above 26x if new assets lift ROCE past 16% without fresh FDA setbacks.

web_blocks.html: Sum-of-the-Parts & Capital-Efficiency Sensitivity: Core US/Europe generics and APIs warrant 18x–20x normalized earnings. Upon FDA clearance and CDMO scaling, Eugia injectables and CuraTeQ/TheraNym biologics merit 25x–28x [1][3][17]. Applying a blended 23.5x multiple to FY28E base EPS of ₹80.00 (on audited 31% tax) yields ₹1,880.00 [1]. At ₹1,845.70 CMP, upside is +1.86% against -14.12% stop risk (0.13:1 R/R). Even at the ₹1,705.36–₹1,749.50 support zone, upside to ₹1,880.00 yields just 0.79:1 R/R against the ₹1,585.12 stop—failing our 1.50:1 hurdle [23]. If Eugia's Warning Letters freeze launches, 18x on ₹74.00 EPS points to ₹1,332.00 [1][8][9].

Valuation Decision Trigger: Because neither ₹1,845.70 CMP (0.13:1 R/R) nor the ₹1,705.36–₹1,749.50 support zone (0.79:1 R/R) clears our 1.50:1 hurdle against ₹1,880.00 fair value, new capital is REJECTED on valuation [23]. USFDA OAI/WL clearance at Eugia Unit III/I shifts fair value toward the ₹2,380.00 bull case [8][9]. An Import Alert or daily close below ₹1,585.12 triggers an immediate exit of held shares [8][9][23].

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have finished our price-blind forensic audit of Aurobindo Pharma's factories, cash flows, and regulatory risks, let's finally open the price ticker and ask the most important valuation question: why does the market value this business at ₹1,845.70 per share today?

At ₹1,845.70—with the official session ledger close on November 13 sitting at ₹1,823.20—Aurobindo carries a market capitalization of ₹1,06,212 crore. Subtract its ₹3,002 crore in net cash and you arrive at an enterprise value of roughly ₹1,03,210 crore. Against trailing twelve-month earnings, the stock trades at 26.1 times P/E, 2.69 times its ₹685 book value, and a tiny 0.38% dividend yield. Notice immediately what happened over the past year: the stock climbed 52.5% from a 52-week low of ₹1,106 to within a whisker of its ₹1,859.90 high. That tells us the easy deep-value re-rating—when investors bought Aurobindo at 12 to 15 times depressed trough earnings—is already behind us.

Yet look across the Indian pharmaceutical peer table and you see a striking puzzle. Sun Pharma trades at 36.9 times earnings. Cipla trades at 36.5 times. Dr. Reddy's trades at 41.6 times, and pure-play injectable rival Gland Pharma trades at 44.7 times. Why is Aurobindo still priced at a 29% to 42% P/E discount to those large-cap peers?

The answer sits squarely in the return ratios and the FDA ledger we examined in Chapters 4 and 6. Sun Pharma earns a 20.5% ROCE backed by a patented specialty portfolio. Aurobindo earns a 12.9% ROCE and a 10.1% ROE because ₹24,902 crore of gross fixed assets and capital work-in-progress are still ramping up, 326 days of inventory sit on the balance sheet, and two of Eugia's key sterile injectable plants—Unit III and Unit I—carry active USFDA Warning Letters. The market is rational: it refuses to pay a 37-times compounder multiple for a 13%-ROCE industrial builder until sterile remediation and asset turns are proven.

Let's run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow test on ₹1,845.70 to see exactly what future the current stock price already assumes. Using an 11.5% cost of capital and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, an enterprise value of ₹1,03,210 crore requires Aurobindo to compound revenue at roughly 10.8% to 11.5% annually over the next decade while sustaining 20.5% to 21.5% operating EBITDA margins and moderating capex-to-sales toward 6.5% to 7.5% once TheraNym Unit 2 is built. Put differently, today's price already bakes in the assumption that Q2 FY27's record ₹10,263 crore quarter is not a one-off spike, that Kakinada Pen-G scales smoothly toward 12,000 metric tonnes, and that Europe and CuraTeQ keep compounding.

That is why our business-quality classification—CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with a WATCH on KPIs—matters so much here. Using audited 31% tax on ₹6,680 crore of FY28E pre-tax profit (₹8,800 crore EBITDA plus ₹450 crore other income minus ₹2,150 crore depreciation and ₹420 crore interest) yields ₹4,609 crore in net profit, or ₹80.02 (~₹80.00) per share across 57.6 crore shares. Applying a 23.5-times multiple gives a base-case fair value of ₹1,880.00. At ₹1,845.70, that is just 1.86% upside against 14.12% stop risk—a 0.13-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Even on a pullback to the ₹1,705.36–₹1,749.50 support zone, upside to ₹1,880.00 is only 0.79-to-1 against the ₹1,585.12 stop, still failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle.

Let's unpack the Reverse DCF numbers a little further so you can feel the sensitivity in your bones. Suppose Aurobindo grows revenue at 11% annually for the next decade—from ₹33,653 crore in FY26 to roughly ₹95,000 crore by FY36—and holds an operating EBITDA margin of 21%. That sounds straightforward until you look at the denominator: invested capital. Between FY21 and FY26, Aurobindo poured over ₹17,000 crore into plants, equipment, and working capital, pushing gross fixed assets and CWIP to ₹24,902 crore. If revenue grows 11% a year without requiring another massive capex wave, depreciation as a percentage of sales gradually falls, free cash flow surges past ₹5,000 crore annually, and ROCE climbs back from 12.9% toward 18%. In that world, ₹1,845.70 looks cheap.

Now test the opposite sensitivity. What if US oral-solid price deflation returns at mid-single digits once gRevlimid exclusivity finishes tapering, forcing Aurobindo to keep spending 8%–9% of sales on capex and R&D just to defend market share? Or what if carrying 326 days of inventory across 150 countries means every ₹100 of incremental revenue swallows ₹35 of incremental working capital? In that slower-turn world, free cash flow stays choppy, ROCE hovers around 11%–13%, and a 26.1-times P/E multiple leaves you exposed to multiple compression toward 18 times.

Look again at the peer comparison table to see how unforgiving the market can be on capital efficiency. Gland Pharma trades at 44.7 times earnings because pure-play sterile injectables historically earn higher margins with cleaner asset turns—though even Gland has faced sharp cyclical drawdowns. Dr. Reddy's trades at 41.6 times with a 13.0% ROCE, supported by a broader branded and emerging-markets mix. Sun Pharma sits at 36.9 times with a 20.5% ROCE because its specialty dermatology and ophthalmology franchise creates genuine pricing power. And Lupin—our outside watchlist benchmark—trades at just 16.3 times earnings despite a 29.9% ROCE and 28.7% ROE, proving that even high-ROCE pharma names get discounted when their chart is stuck in Stage 1 consolidation.

For Aurobindo, the valuation takeaway is crystal clear. At ₹1,845.70, the stock is already priced at full value for a smooth handoff from heavy construction to profitable utilization. Our ₹1,880.00 base target implies just 1.86% upside over 18–24 months—nowhere near enough to clear our 1.50-to-1 asymmetry hurdle at CMP (0.13-to-1) or even at support (0.79-to-1).

Let's check one more nuance in our valuation work: why historical multiple bands matter for a cyclical-conditional pharma business. Back in FY15–FY18, when Aurobindo was earning 23%–27% ROCE on a much smaller fixed-asset base, the market routinely valued the stock at 18x to 24x forward earnings. During the FY22–FY23 margin trough, that multiple compressed to 11x–15x. Today, at 26.1x trailing earnings and roughly 15.0x EV/EBITDA, the market is already giving Aurobindo partial credit for Q2 FY27's ₹10,263 crore revenue breakout.

To earn a sustained multiple above 26x—say toward 28x–30x like higher-ROCE peers—Aurobindo has to prove that its ₹24,902 crore fixed-asset and CWIP base can generate >16% ROCE without another working-capital bloat. Until that proof arrives in audited quarterly numbers, paying 26.1x at the top of a 52-week rally leaves little room for error.

Notice one more subtle point in our sum-of-the-parts check: why investors should not lazily apply a 35-times Sun Pharma multiple to Aurobindo's consolidated earnings. Aurobindo's core US and European oral-solid generics and bulk APIs are scale businesses, not patented specialty franchises; on their own, they warrant 18x to 20x normalized earnings. The re-rating upside comes from Eugia sterile injectables, CuraTeQ biosimilars, and TheraNym CDMO earning higher multiples as they scale—which blends fairly to our 23.5x FY28E EPS base multiple of ₹1,880.00.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: At 26.1x TTM P/E (26.8x on TradingView), Aurobindo already prices in an 11% revenue CAGR and 21% margins. With audited 31% tax yielding ₹80.00 FY28E EPS and a ₹1,880.00 base fair value, new capital cannot clear our 1.50:1 hurdle even on a pullback to support.
